author: claude
subject: Thread verdict
body:
The prerequisite is met, and the separation the fix introduces is better than the one the finding asked for.

`discover_blob_paths` now returns two things instead of one: the **trusted** logical blob, established only when the head's signature validates, and an untrusted **routing hint** — a canonical logical blob whose SHA-256 matches the head key. The lease routes on the hint, the reconciliation acts on the trusted value, and `reconcile_head_locked` receives `blob.as_ref()` rather than the hint. An unverifiable head can therefore determine where a lease is taken and nothing else; it cannot be promoted to committed state.

That distinction matters because the naive fix — route everything to `replicas[0]` of whatever the head claims — would have let a forged head choose a lease target. Deriving the hint from the head key's hash rather than from its contents makes lease placement and lock key consistent by construction: `locks/{path_hash}` is taken on the primary of the blob whose `path_hash` that is, which is exactly the lease the Gateway would take for the same blob.

The `ensure!` guard is the right complement. When a trusted blob exists, discovery outside its active Ring placement fails closed rather than proceeding on a backend the blob is not assigned to.

**The residual is sound and is now stated.** A head that identifies no canonical logical blob stays on its discovery backend, because there is no Gateway-owned logical state for it to contend with. ADR-0012's wording already scopes the canonical lease to components that write Gateway-owned commit state, so the exception is consistent with the record rather than an unrecorded carve-out. The implementation-status section says so explicitly.

`reconciler/src/engine/tests/orchestration.rs::anomalous_head_discovered_on_secondary_locks_deterministic_primary` is the regression that keeps it true, and it exercises the case that motivated the finding: a head present only on the secondary, unverifiable, acquiring the lease on the primary and being quarantined.

**What this unblocks.** The amendment to ADR-0010 now holds: with both components excluding one another on identifiable blobs, Reconciler-owned quarantine and compaction state cannot change inside a commit, so the write path may read each once per replica per request instead of twice. That is roughly four of the twenty-eight control reads on a first `PUT`, and the same treatment applied to Gateway-owned documents takes it to about ten — none of which requires the merged document itself.

**What this verdict does not cover.** Methods: source review only. No commands executed; no cargo toolchain is available in this environment. Seq 2 names `cargo test -p overmesh-reconciler`, `cargo test --workspace`, clippy, `make doc-check` and `git diff --check`; those runs are unconfirmed here and falsifiable by anyone who repeats them.
